title: Writing: Email Purpose and Structure
focus: Abrir, contextualizar e concluir e-mails acadêmicos

content.text: abertura, contexto, conteúdo (os pontos pedidos) e fechamento
Ao final da aula você consegue:
escrever um e-mail claro de 100–150 palavras pedindo informações.
Who do you write emails to in your daily life?
How do you start and end a formal email in Portuguese? And in English?
Have you ever received a confusing email? Why was it confusing?
Dear Professor Smith, · Dear Dr. Lee, · Dear Admissions Office, · To whom it may concern,
Hello Ms. Garcia, · Hi Professor Lee,
Contexto (1ª frase — quem é você e por que escreve)
My name is… and I'm a second-year student in…
I'm writing to ask about / to inquire about…
I'm interested in… and I'd like some information about…
Thank you in advance for your help.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Please let me know if you need any further information.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Thank you in advance, and I look forward to hearing from you.

content.text: (1–2 frases): quem você é + por que escreve.
Leia o enunciado como um checklist

You are interested in a summer research program at your university. Write an email to the program coordinator. In your email: (1) introduce yourself, (2) explain why you are interested, (3) ask about requirements and dates.
✔ Cada item vira uma parte do e-mail.
My name is Camila Rocha, and I'm a second-year biology student. I'm writing to ask about the summer research program in the Ecology Lab.
I'm very interested in the program because I'd like to gain hands-on experience with field research. Last semester, I took Professor Lima's ecology course, and I really enjoyed the lab sessions.
Could you please tell me what the requirements are to apply? I'd also like to know when the program starts and whether students need to stay on campus during the summer.
Thank you in advance for your help. I look forward to hearing from you.
(≈ 120 palavras) O aluno lê em voz alta como se ditasse o e-mail.
4.1 Troque e fale: frases de contexto

→ a third-year economics student / inquire about internship opportunities → a graduate student in history / request access to the archives → an exchange student from Brazil / ask about housing options
4.2 Transforme em pergunta educada (oral e escrito)
I want to know about the course of English. How much is it? When it starts? Waiting your answer.

content.text: You saw a poster about a free weekend workshop on academic writing at the campus Writing Center. Write an email to the Writing Center. In your email:
introduce yourself and say how you learned about the workshop,
explain why you want to attend,
ask two questions about the workshop.
B. Revisão em voz alta — 5 min
O aluno lê o e-mail. O professor verifica o checklist abaixo e o aluno corrige
[ ] Contexto na primeira frase (quem sou + por que escrevo)?
[ ] Todos os 3 pontos do enunciado cobertos?
Copie 10 frases úteis da aula (abertura, contexto, pedido, fechamento) e memorize.
Reescreva o e-mail do Lucas de forma correta e educada.
Write to a language school asking about evening classes (level test, price, schedule).
Use o checklist da seção 6 para revisar o e-mail do dia 3.
Grave-se lendo o modelo da Camila com entonação natural. Depois explique em 30 s o que ela pede.
Write to a professor asking if you can attend her class as a visitor.

questions.questionText: What should the first sentence of an academic email usually contain?

options.text: Who you are and why you are writing
A long story about your life

explanations.general: Correct answer: Who you are and why you are writing

questions.questionText: I look forward to ______ from you. (hear)

explanations.general: I look forward to hearing from you.

questions.questionText: Which closing is appropriate for a professor?

options.text: Could you please tell me what the requirements are?
Could you please tell me what are the requirements?
Could you please tell me the requirements are what?

explanations.general: Correct answer: Could you please tell me what the requirements are?

questions.questionText: To whom it may ______, (abertura quando não se sabe o nome)
If the prompt asks for three points, you can skip one if your email is long enough.

explanations.general: Falso: inclua todos os pontos pedidos.

content.text: 1 Could you please tell me what the requirements are? 2 I'd like to know whether there is a fee. 3 I was also wondering when it starts. 4 Would it be possible to apply late?

saudação informal e com primeiro nome; sem contexto; “course of English” → “English course”; perguntas diretas (e “When it starts?” errada → “When does it start?”); “Waiting your answer” → “I look forward to hearing from you”; “Bye” → “Best regards”.
